title: U.S. House · Connecticut's 5th District
area: Northwestern and north-central Connecticut, including Waterbury, Danbury, New Britain, and Torrington

context.text: The Democratic primary was canceled and incumbent Jahana Hayes advanced without appearing on the ballot. Chris Shea defeated Jonathan De Barros in the Republican primary, winning 81% of the vote. The Cook Political Report rated this district D+3 based on 2024 presidential results, making it the most competitive of Connecticut's five U.S. House seats.

summary.text: Jahana Hayes is the Democratic incumbent for Connecticut's 5th Congressional District, first elected in 2018. A Waterbury native, she taught history for 15 years and was named 2016 National Teacher of the Year before running for Congress. She serves on the House Agriculture and Education and Workforce committees.

background.text: Born in Waterbury, Connecticut, in 1973; her official biography describes Waterbury as her hometown.

Earned an associate degree from Naugatuck Valley Community College (2002), a bachelor's degree from Southern Connecticut State University (2005), a master's degree in curriculum and instruction from the University of Saint Joseph (2012), and an advanced degree in educational administration and supervision from the University of Bridgeport (2014).
Taught history for 15 years at John F. Kennedy High School in Waterbury, where she was named Waterbury Teacher of the Year and Connecticut Teacher of the Year.
Named 2016 National Teacher of the Year, and in that role traveled the country and the world as an ambassador for public education.

Elected to the U.S. House in November 2018, defeating Republican Manny Santos, 55.9% to 44.1%; her office describes her as the first African-American woman to represent Connecticut in Congress. She took office in 2019 and is serving her fourth term.

Serves on the House Committee on Education and Workforce and the House Agriculture Committee, where she is ranking member of the Subcommittee on Nutrition and Foreign Agriculture. In the 117th Congress she chaired the Agriculture subcommittee on Nutrition, Oversight, and Department Operations.
According to her official biography, she has had 11 bills signed into law and has introduced 80 bills.

priorities.text: Says she has been a strong proponent of "commonsense gun laws that keeps our communities safe," supporting universal background checks, community violence prevention funding, and safe storage.

Says her work has centered on "reducing systemic barriers to healthcare that cause disparities, while increasing access and affordability," including lowering drug prices and stabilizing the Affordable Care Act.
Says she has introduced proposals to "mitigate carbon emissions and conserve our ecosystems, while creating high-wage, union jobs," and has been an original cosponsor of the Green New Deal.

positions.summary: Says she has supported legislation for universal background checks, community violence prevention funding, and safe storage, and serves as Deputy Whip on the Gun Violence Prevention Task Force.
positions.quote: She has supported legislation for universal background checks, community violence prevention funding, and safe storage.

positions.summary: Says she supported legislation during the COVID-19 pandemic to expand insurance and provide emergency coverage to people who lost coverage, and has supported legislation to strengthen Medicare and Medicaid and lower drug prices.
positions.quote: During the COVID-19 pandemic, Congresswoman Hayes supported legislation that would expand insurance and provide emergency coverage to the millions of individuals who lost coverage.

positions.summary: Has introduced legislation to mitigate carbon emissions, secured billions in federal funding to replace diesel school buses with zero-emissions buses, and has been an original cosponsor of the Green New Deal since her first term.
positions.quote: Since her first term, she has been an original cosponsor of the Green New Deal and knows climate change mitigation must be centered in every policy Congress considers.

positions.summary: Says she has advocated for the expansion of protections for renters through the pandemic and supports the Build Back Better Act's investments in affordable housing and rental assistance.
positions.quote: Congresswoman Hayes has advocated for the expansion of protections for renters, landlords and homeowners though the pandemic.

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on Agriculture and the Committee on Education and the Workforce in the 2025–2026 Congress.
Chaired the Agriculture Subcommittee on Nutrition, Oversight, and Department Operations in the 2021–2022 Congress.
Served as ranking member of the Agriculture Subcommittee on Nutrition, Foreign Agriculture, and Horticulture in the 2023–2024 Congress.
Introduced the Clean School Bus Act and Clean Commute for Kids Act and negotiated $5 billion for these proposals in the bipartisan Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act.

candidates.name: Chris Shea
candidates.ballotNote: Defeated Jonathan De Barros in the August 11, 2026 Republican primary

summary.text: Chris Shea is the Republican nominee for Connecticut's 5th Congressional District, having won the August 11, 2026 Republican primary. According to his campaign website, he is a Watertown native, retired Navy SEAL with more than 30 years of service, firefighter and nonprofit founder. His campaign materials cite lowering costs and cutting federal spending among his goals.

background.text: According to his campaign website, he is a Watertown native who grew up in Watertown.
According to his campaign website, he earned a Bachelor of Science from Charter Oak State College and was commissioned a Navy Warrant Officer in 2012.

According to his campaign website, he began his Navy career in 1991 as a hospital corpsman, completed Basic Underwater Demolition/SEAL (BUD/S) and Special Forces Medic training, and served with SEAL Team 8, SEAL Team 18, Naval Special Warfare Group Two, the Naval Special Warfare Development Group and Special Operations Command North, and at the Pentagon.

His campaign website says he deployed to Afghanistan, took part in a 1997 special operations mission in the former Yugoslavia, and from 2014 to 2016 served in Mexico, including at the U.S. Embassy in Mexico City, training Mexican special operations forces. He retired from the Navy in January 2024.
According to his campaign website, he has been a firefighter since 2009 and is a lieutenant with the North Haven Fire Department.

According to his campaign website, he founded and is president of Hero to Hero, Inc., a nonprofit that helps special operations veterans and other service members move into first-responder careers, and he previously owned a handyman business with six employees.

Won the August 11, 2026 Republican primary over Jonathan De Barros, 81.0% to 19.0%. According to his campaign website, he lives in Cheshire with his wife, Anita; they raised their daughter, Sophia, in Watertown.
